In brief: The upcoming week in Abuja will be characterized by a persistent low-pressure system that will bring widespread rainfall and high humidity levels, with temperatures ranging from 21°C to 29°C throughout the week. ### Monday The low-pressure system currently situated over the city will continue to dominate the weather pattern, leading to a high chance of rain throughout the day. Temperatures will reach a high of 29°C, while the low will be 22°C, with a relative humidity of 61% and a UV index of 0. The rain is expected to be most intense during the late afternoon and evening hours, with accumulation ranges predicted to be between 10-20 mm. Residents in low-lying areas such as Gwarinpa and certain parts of Maitama should be prepared for potential flooding. The wind will be relatively calm, blowing at 6 km/h, which will contribute to the high humidity levels.
The high humidity will make the temperature feel more like 26°C, even in the shade. This will be particularly noticeable in areas with high population density, such as Wuse and Garki. The rain will also lead to reduced visibility, especially during the evening commute, so drivers should exercise caution when traveling on roads such as the Nnamdi Azikiwe Expressway. The current light traffic conditions will likely deteriorate as the rain becomes more intense. As the day progresses, the rain will become more widespread, covering most areas of the city, including the airport road and the vicinity of Aso Rock. The National Assembly complex, located in the Three Arms Zone, will also be affected by the rain, which may lead to disruptions in the daily activities. The models suggest that the rain will continue into the night, with a slight decrease in intensity. ### Tuesday The low-pressure system will intensify, leading to an increased chance of rain, with a 86% probability of precipitation throughout the day. The high temperature will remain at 29°C, while the low will be 22°C. The relative humidity will increase to 80%, making the temperature feel even more oppressive. The UV index will remain at 0, indicating that there will be no significant sun exposure. The wind direction will shift slightly, blowing at 8 km/h from the southwest, which will contribute to the increased humidity levels.
The rain will be more intense than the previous day, with accumulation ranges predicted to be between 20-30 mm. This will lead to more severe flooding in low-lying areas, and residents should take necessary precautions to protect themselves and their properties. The high humidity will also lead to fog formation in certain areas, particularly during the early morning hours. The fog will be most dense in areas with high vegetation, such as the vicinity of the National Arboretum. As the day progresses, the rain will become even more widespread, covering the entire city, including the outskirts. The models suggest that the rain will continue into the night, with a high chance of thunderstorms. The thunderstorms will be accompanied by strong winds, which may lead to power outages and disruptions in communication services. ### Wednesday The low-pressure system will reach its peak intensity, leading to a 90% chance of rain throughout the day. The high temperature will remain at 29°C, while the low will drop to 21°C. The relative humidity will increase further, reaching 85%, making the temperature feel even more uncomfortable. The UV index will remain at 0, indicating that there will be no significant sun exposure. The wind direction will shift again, blowing at 10 km/h from the southeast, which will contribute to the increased humidity levels.
The rain will be the most intense of the week, with accumulation ranges predicted to be between 30-40 mm. This will lead to severe flooding in low-lying areas, and residents should take all necessary precautions to protect themselves and their properties. The high humidity will also lead to fog formation in certain areas, particularly during the early morning hours. The fog will be most dense in areas with high vegetation, such as the vicinity of the National Arboretum. As the day progresses, the rain will become even more widespread, covering the entire city, including the outskirts. The models suggest that the rain will continue into the night, with a high chance of thunderstorms. The thunderstorms will be accompanied by strong winds, which may lead to power outages and disruptions in communication services. My best guess is that the rain will start to decrease in intensity by the late evening hours, but the high humidity will persist. ### Thursday The low-pressure system will start to weaken, leading to a decrease in the chance of rain, with a 73% probability of precipitation throughout the day. The high temperature will drop to 28°C, while the low will rise to 22°C. The relative humidity will decrease slightly, reaching 80%, making the temperature feel slightly more comfortable. The UV index will remain at 0, indicating that there will be no significant sun exposure. The wind direction will shift again, blowing at 8 km/h from the northwest, which will contribute to the decreased humidity levels. The rain will be less intense than the previous day, with accumulation ranges predicted to be between 10-20 mm. This will lead to a decrease in flooding in low-lying areas, and residents can start to resume their normal activities. The high humidity will still lead to fog formation in certain areas, particularly during the early morning hours. The fog will be most dense in areas with high vegetation, such as the vicinity of the National Arboretum. As the day progresses, the rain will become less widespread, covering only certain areas of the city. The models suggest that the rain will continue into the night, but with a lower chance of thunderstorms. The wind will be relatively calm, blowing at 6 km/h, which will contribute to the decreased humidity levels. There's a chance that the rain will clear up by the early morning hours of the next day, leading to a relatively dry morning. ### Friday The low-pressure system will continue to weaken, leading to a further decrease in the chance of rain, with a 76% probability of precipitation throughout the day. The high temperature will remain at 28°C, while the low will drop to 21°C. The relative humidity will decrease further, reaching 75%, making the temperature feel even more comfortable. The UV index will remain at 0, indicating that there will be no significant sun exposure. The wind direction will shift again, blowing at 10 km/h from the northeast, which will contribute to the decreased humidity levels. The rain will be even less intense than the previous day, with accumulation ranges predicted to be between 5-10 mm. This will lead to a significant decrease in flooding in low-lying areas, and residents can resume their normal activities without any disruptions. The high humidity will still lead to fog formation in certain areas, particularly during the early morning hours. The fog will be most dense in areas with high vegetation, such as the vicinity of the National Arboretum. As the day progresses, the rain will become even less widespread, covering only certain areas of the city. The models suggest that the rain will clear up by the late evening hours, leading to a relatively dry night. The wind will be relatively calm, blowing at 6 km/h, which will contribute to the decreased humidity levels. My best guess is that the rain will return by the next day, but with a lower chance of intense precipitation. One practical takeaway for residents is to be prepared for potential flooding in low-lying areas, especially during the peak intensity of the low-pressure system, and to plan their daily activities accordingly, taking into account the high humidity and reduced visibility due to the rain and fog.
